rootCause.cause: The previous runtime queue contained only NarrationContract's fixed 9 sentences. It completed about 93.819 seconds after screen-off while the foreground service kept the process and notification alive for the remainder of the 30-minute observation.

MIUI SystemUI maps Notification.MediaStyle to a fixed previous/play-pause/next transport row and ignored both app action order and the fourth stop action. Reordering compact actions alone was not sufficient.
The previous candidate had a real focus request but no independent package/UID audio owner to trigger a genuine OS focus-loss callback. Same-process simulation was not acceptable evidence.
Terminal TTS states persisted through publishState but did not demote the foreground service or remove its notification automatically.

experience: A MediaStyle notification's action order is not a reliable cross-OEM control layout. On the tested MIUI build, SystemUI derived previous/play-pause/next from the media surface and hid stop; a custom RemoteViews notification was required to make all four actions visible.
Exact current-notification checks must match NotificationRecord records, not historical notification dump text.
PowerShell automatic variable $pid must not carry runtime PIDs; use a task-specific variable such as runtimePid.
A host-side filtered logcat file is required for multi-minute audio evidence because the device main buffer rotates.
Terminal playback states must demote foreground/notification explicitly; service survival alone is not playback continuity.
